Consistency.justification: The proposal aligns perfectly with the provided core idea, capturing all required elements including the Locomamba framework, selective state-space fusion (MAMBA), proprioceptive and depth encoders, end-to-end PPO training, domain randomization, and obstacle curriculum. It also directly responds to the gaps identified in the literature review, such as the quadratic scaling cost of transformers.

Clarity.justification: The research proposal is exceptionally clear and structured. The methodology provides precise details, including network layer dimensions, specific window sizes for the MAMBA layers, exact PPO hyperparameters, and distinct components of the reward function. The experimental setup and baselines are also unambiguously defined.

Novelty.justification: While MAMBA itself is an existing architecture, adapting it for cross-modal fusion (proprioception and exteroceptive depth) in high-frequency, end-to-end continuous control for quadruped locomotion is highly innovative. It offers a fresh perspective to solve the long-horizon, memory-intensive bottlenecks of standard Transformer-based locomotion policies.

Soundness.justification: The proposed approach is technically rigorous and well-founded. The experimental design is particularly strong, featuring matched-compute comparisons, multiplicity-corrected statistical testing, and a comprehensive set of baselines. The methodology sensibly employs auxiliary task gating to prevent gradient interference. A minor omission is the lack of specificity regarding the target physics simulator (e.g., Isaac Gym) and robotic hardware platform.

Feasibility.justification: The proposal is highly practical. The use of MAMBA's near-linear time and memory scaling makes the ambitious latency targets (p50 < 6 ms) achievable on constrained onboard hardware. The sim-to-real transfer plan is pragmatic, utilizing lightweight residual adapters and rigorous domain randomization, though real-world deployment always carries inherent hardware risks which the proposal aptly acknowledges.

Significance.justification: Vision-based quadrupedal locomotion is a highly active and challenging research area. By successfully reducing the latency and memory footprint of spatial-temporal sequence modeling, this framework would allow robots to process longer horizons and higher-resolution inputs onboard, leading to a meaningful advancement in the autonomy and safety of legged robots.

strengths: Exceptional level of methodological detail, including explicit hyperparameters, reward structures, and architectural dimensions.
Rigorous and robust experimental protocol, including strict matched-compute baselines, predefined statistical tests, and numerous ablation studies.
Novel and highly practical application of the MAMBA architecture to solve a critical bottleneck (attention scaling) in vision-driven locomotion.
weaknesses: Fails to specify the exact physics simulator (e.g., Isaac Gym, MuJoCo) and the physical quadruped hardware platform (e.g., ANYmal, Unitree Go1) that will be used for validation.

The assumption that MAMBA's linear-time recurrence will easily stabilize across highly disparate modalities (depth vs. proprioception) might require more complex fusion mechanisms than standard stacking.
